reported_symptom: Loot chat announces an item that cannot be found in the inventory; screenshot shows Soathova pečeť (+67).
root_cause: CS_GETITEM_ACK included a leading item-slot byte, but OnCS_GETITEM_ACK reads SetItemData and SetItemMagic directly. The extra byte shifted the item identity and every following field. Inventory ADD/UPDATE packets already have the correct separate layout.

screenshot_reproduction.explanation: The blue herb merges into the existing bag stack; the broken announcement describes a different item. No seal was granted or lost in this reproduction.

inspected: git log and 34a9afe original GETITEM sender diff/blame
Current uncommitted quest-acquisition hook diff and QuestLootEventTests
ItemLootTests, InventoryCapacityTests and existing item packet serializer
history_review.reason_for_change: All six regression scenarios independently decoded the old announcement as template 15104 instead of 17211. This reproduces the screenshot exactly and agrees with the actual client reader; the C++ sender also explicitly omits the slot.
history_review.preserved: Quest acquisition hooks, pickup permissions, inventory persistence, chart capacity, ADD/UPDATE slot prefixes, response order and existing party-lottery fixes. No balance, loot-rate or SQL-content changes.

protocol_evidence: Client/TClient/CSHandler.cpp: OnCS_GETITEM_ACK versus OnCS_ADDITEM_ACK and OnCS_MONITEMTAKE_ACK

validation.cases: Individual pickup, take all and asynchronous two-player lottery; each into an empty slot and an existing stack. Decode the complete native item-data block, assert packet exhaustion and verify ADD/UPDATE still contain bag and slot bytes.
validation.deployed_library_method: Copy the five production assemblies from the recreated running container into an isolated copy of the built test output, then execute LootNotificationTests with dotnet vstest.
